title: Comparisons That Rank Honestly
objective: After this lesson you will be able to rank categories with sorted bars (zero baselines, value labels, uncertainty where it matters) and choose grouped vs stacked layouts by the comparison question.
why: Unsorted bars hide rankings, truncated axes exaggerate gaps, missing values sort arbitrarily — comparison charts fail more often in framing than in data. Sorted position-encoded bars with zero baselines and labeled values make magnitudes undeniable; grouped-vs-stacked choice follows whether the question compares across or within groups.

blocks.text: Three non-negotiables: **sort descending** (rank readable without eye-measuring), **zero baseline** (bar length ∝ value — truncation lies ratios), **value labels** (exact numbers beside bars for the precise readers). Unsorted bars force O(n²) eye comparisons; sorted bars answer rank in one glance.

blocks.caption: Sort + label + qualify: rank readable, precision honest

blocks.text: Grouped vs stacked: across or within

**Grouped bars** compare across categories within series (Q3 across regions — side-by-side lengths). **Stacked bars** compose totals within categories (region mix per quarter — parts + whole). Wrong choice hides the asked comparison: stacked obscures cross-group ranks (baselines shift); grouped obscures totals. Question wording decides ('across regions' → grouped; 'mix within' → stacked).

blocks.title: Small multiples scale comparisons
blocks.text: Beyond ~8 categories, single charts crowd: small multiples (one mini-chart per group, shared scales) preserve readability where mega-charts collapse. Same scales across panels, or comparisons lie by framing.

blocks.title: Rank the categories
blocks.note: Run it: expect 1.shoes,2.hats,3.apparel with leader margin 158. Sorted once, rank readable instantly — the one-line difference between data and insight.

items: Sort descending + zero baseline + value labels: rank in one glance, ratios honest
Grouped compares across (shared baselines); stacked composes within (totals + mix)
Flag small-n bars: rank shown, trust qualified

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice ranking and confirm order + margin. (b) Reorder input (apparel first) and confirm identical output (sort stability vs input order). (c) Choose grouped vs stacked for 'Q3 share across regions' vs 'regional mix within Q3' with one-line reasons.
hints: Input order irrelevant post-sort: ranking derives from values (order-independence proven).
Across regions → grouped (shared baselines compare); mix within → stacked (totals + parts together).
exercise.why: Order-independence (sort erases input bias), margin reporting (gaps quantified), and layout-by-question (grouped/stacked semantics) are the three comparison judgments.
exercise.code: // Comparison pattern: sort desc, zero baseline, label values, flag thin.

quiz.q: Unsorted bars, truncated axis, no labels. Fix order?
options: Sort desc + zero baseline + value labels (rank, ratios, precision — in that repair order)
quiz.explain: Each repair fixes a lie class: order (rank), baseline (ratios), labels (precision). Cosmetics after honesty, never before.

quiz.q: 'Regional mix within Q3' as grouped bars. Issue?
options: Wrong layout: within-composition needs stacked (totals + parts); grouped serves across-comparisons
quiz.explain: Layout follows the question's preposition: within→stacked, across→grouped. Mismatches hide the asked comparison.

options: Rank shown with thin-data flag: position earned, trust qualified (small samples wobble)
quiz.explain: Rank and reliability separate: show the order, flag the evidence weight. Hidden uncertainty misleads more than shown weakness.

summary: Sorted, zero-based, labeled, layout-matched comparisons with thin-data flags. Rank readable, ratios honest, questions answered.
